speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how long you've had this painful ulcer on your leg, and did you recall any injury or bite before it appeared?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you noticed any other symptoms such as fever, joint pain, or new rashes elsewhere on your body? Given your history of Crohn's disease and uveitis, are you currently taking any immunosuppressive medications?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Painful ulcerative lesion on the right leg. I also have Lesion has a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders, History of ant bite at the site of the lesion, Pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities, Dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any history of varicose veins or deep vein thrombosis, and have you noticed any new fever or chills since the lesion appeared? REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count and Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Vital Signs: Temperature 37.6°C (98°F), Pulse 98/min, Blood Pressure 126/88 mm Hg. Skin Examination: 4-cm tender ulcerative lesion on anterior right leg with central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders; pitting pedal edema; dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs. Complete Blood Count: WBC Normal, Hemoglobin Normal, Platelets Normal. Blood Glucose Level: Random Elevated. Skin Biopsy Histopathology: Neutrophilic infiltration without infection, consistent with pyoderma gangrenosum. Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate: NORMAL READINGS.

speaker: Doctor
text: The biopsy showing neutrophilic infiltration without infection confirms this is pyoderma gangrenosum, likely triggered by the ant bite and associated with your Crohn's disease. Given the normal ESR and elevated glucose, I will proceed to confirm the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyoderma Gangrenosum.
